title: Enrollment Endings and Changes to Fulfilment or Sync Day — Auto Refill & Medication Sync
content:
The patient may stop an Auto Refill & Medication Sync enrollment at any time. Stopping is the patient's own request and does not cancel a cycle already dispensed.

## Stopping at the patient's request

An enrollment in enrolled, active or paused status moves to unenrolled when the patient stops it, with the reason patient request and the date stopped as its closing date. Stopping from enrolled status is the patient withdrawing before the first cycle.

## Endings by the program

The program ends an enrollment — moving it to ended status, with the date ended as its closing date and the reason recorded — in these cases:

| Reason recorded | The program ends the enrollment when |
|---|---|
| Prescription closed | Its prescription expires, is transferred out or is discontinued |
| Consecutive unpicked | The run of automated fills returned to stock unpicked reaches the program's unpicked-fill limit |
| Program change | The patient's prescriptions move into a Med Sync group |
| Consent not renewed | Annual renewal of consent was required and not given |
| Pause expired | A pause ends the enrollment under the pausing terms |

**Counting the unpicked run.** The run is taken over the enrollment's filled cycles, most recent first, stopping at the first one whose fill was picked up; it is the number of those filled cycles whose fill was returned to stock under Prescriptions.

Worked run (hypothetical inputs, with the program's unpicked-fill limit taken as 2):

| Filled cycles, most recent first | Unpicked run | Limit reached |
|---|---|---|
| returned to stock, returned to stock, picked up | 2 | Yes — ended as consecutive unpicked |
| returned to stock, picked up, returned to stock | 1 | No |

## Changing fulfilment or sync day

A patient may change the fulfilment method to another of the methods the program offers and, for a Med Sync enrollment, the sync day under the sync-group rules. Either change takes effect from the next unprocessed cycle.

Example (hypothetical): a patient changes from store pickup to home delivery when the next cycle has already been processed. That cycle keeps store pickup; the change takes effect from the first cycle not yet processed.

## Points of judgement

- **Who stops, and what status results?** The patient's own request gives unenrolled; an ending by the program gives ended.
- **Does stopping undo a dispensed cycle?** No; a cycle already dispensed is not cancelled.
- **From when does a change of fulfilment method or sync day apply?** From the next unprocessed cycle.
